verdicts.claim: both objects exist as trapped vibrations with rate above the ceiling 2 (C-grid, G1)
verdicts.rule: 2.3 C1: periodic solution to solver precision with rate > 2, and 'trapped' by 2.1 (frac >= 0.90 at 1,000 cycles, twin <= 0.50, rate above 2 by more than the spectral resolution)
verdicts.measured: sbend: family of 21 points, rate 2.01 to 4.316, worst period-return error 1.12e-11; trapped (2.1) at 6 of 6 lifetime rates (2.05, 2.2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4.2); bump: family of 24 points, rate 2.01 to 4.916, worst period-return error 2.51e-12; trapped (2.1) at 5 of 6 lifetime rates (2.05, 2.2, 2.5, 3, 3.5)
verdicts.threshold: period-return error < 1e-8; rate > 2; trapped at >= 1 lifetime rate per object

verdicts.claim: C-grid, G2: S-bend stable and unchanged past 32,000 cycles; bump unstable and moves
verdicts.measured: not run in WP-C (the production runs use G1 only, as the task states)
verdicts.note: The WP-B1 build regression (not a production run) is in docs/WPB1_BUILD_NOTES.md section 10: S-bend multiplier 1 + 8e-15 and frac 0.99999988 at 31,995 cycles (hit); bump multiplier 2.062, centroid 0 -> -0.5 and stays (unstable: hit; moves by >= 1 site: miss). Those numbers are the build's, not re-measured here.

verdicts.claim: same ordering with G1: S-bend stable, bump unstable and moves
verdicts.rule: 2.3 C2/C3: stable = largest Floquet multiplier within 1e-6 of the unit circle AND peak amplitude and centre within 1% (centre read as 0.01 unit) AND fixed-window frac >= 0.99 at 32,000 cycles; unstable-and-moves = multiplier > 1 + 1e-3 AND centroid leaves its site by >= 1 unit with co-moving frac >= 0.90; shift 0.5 to 1 that does not grow is a split (Block 5)
verdicts.measured: S-bend stable at 6 of 6 rates (rates 2.05, 2.2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4.2); bump: unstable and moves at 0, shifts half a site and stays at 2, other at 4 of 6

verdicts.claim: a trapped vibration emits nothing at its rate or overtones; fixed-window energy constant
verdicts.rule: 2.3 C4: drift <= 10 x closed-string conservation error, and no line at the rate or overtones above the leakage floor at a far probe
verdicts.measured: fixed-window drift over 10000 cycles: closed ring 6.01e-12, sponge 5.78e-12; closed-ring conservation error 2.78e-08; ratios 2.16e-04 (closed), 2.08e-04 (sponge). Far-probe lines with (omega A)^2 above 1e-5 E0: none; largest (omega A)^2 over the rate and odd overtones 5.13e-35 against the Block 6 floor 1e-5 E0 = 9.98e-06; line amplitude over the local spectral floor: rate and odd overtones 1.33 to 3.24, symmetry-forbidden even harmonics 1.51 to 2.04 (so the lines are not distinguishable from the floor); exp(-kappa L) = 7.5e-37 at 60 sites
verdicts.threshold: ratio <= 10 (<= 30 pass with note); (omega A)^2 of every line <= 1e-5 E0 (Block 6 floor)
verdicts.note: drift ratio verdict hit; spectrum verdict hit

verdicts.claim: a trapped vibration can be moved with small loss at low speed; loss grows with speed
verdicts.rule: 2.3 C5 (as written): at the lowest push strength the object crosses 100 units with co-moving frac >= 0.90, and loss per unit distance does not decrease from one speed to the next; break speed = lowest measured speed with co-moving frac < 0.5 within 100 units
verdicts.measured: sbend w=2.1: lowest lambda 0.05 does not cross 100 (frac at 100: n/a); loss non-decreasing with speed: False; alt reading (lowest mover lambda 0.1, frac at 100 1); break speed n/a | sbend w=2.3: lowest lambda 0.05 does not cross 100 (frac at 100: n/a); loss non-decreasing with speed: None; alt reading (lowest mover lambda n/a, frac at 100 n/a); break speed n/a | sbend w=3: lowest lambda 0.05 does not cross 100 (frac at 100: n/a); loss non-decreasing with speed: None; alt reading (lowest mover lambda n/a, frac at 100 n/a); break speed n/a | bump w=2.3: lowest lambda 0.05 does not cross 100 (frac at 100: n/a); loss non-decreasing with speed: None; alt reading (lowest mover lambda n/a, frac at 100 n/a); break speed n/a
verdicts.threshold: lowest push crosses 100 with frac >= 0.90; loss non-decreasing
verdicts.note: literal reading applied; the 'alt reading' column gives the lowest push that does move the object. Added after review: S-bend 2.3 and bump 2.3 are not pinned: they move 5 to 20 sites and stop (max excursions 19.8 and 9.4); the speed column is a fit after the first 10% of a long run (diagnostics D1)

verdicts.claim: a swirl has an optimal length and rate and the range is narrow; too long or too fast and it becomes a travelling wave
verdicts.rule: narrow: trapped range < factor 2 in length and in rate; optimal: an interior point has lifetime >= 2x both edges (or, alive at the cap, loss rate <= half); too long: starts longer than the window's upper edge fall below frac 0.50 within 1,000 cycles; too fast: a break speed below 1 exists
verdicts.measured: sbend: trapped 2.05 to 4.2 (x2.05 in rate), L_half 0.5163 to 1.44 (x2.79); narrow=False; interior point with loss <= half of both edges: True | bump: trapped 2.05 to 3.5 (x1.71 in rate), L_half 0.441 to 1.409 (x3.20); narrow=False; interior point with loss <= half of both edges: False | starts longer than the window's upper edge (L_half > 1.44): 9 of them, of which 4 fall below frac 0.50 within 1,000 cycles | break speed (lowest speed with co-moving frac < 0.5 within 100 units): none measured: no push broke the object within 100 units (long-wave speed 1) || clauses: narrow contradicted, optimal split, too long split, too fast contradicted
verdicts.note: clause-by-clause words in the measured column; length range is the C-grid family's L_half at the trapped end rates

verdicts.claim: the S-bend traps energy better than the single bump

verdicts.measured: 5 S-bend runs inside the bump's energy range; S-bend retains more at 5, less at 0; all alive at cap: True; loss rates within 2x at all: False; per point (E: S-bend frac / bump frac interpolated in log E): 0.6282: 1 / 0.9997; 0.9983: 1 / 0.9898; 1.416: 1 / 0.98; 1.798: 1 / 0.9733; 2.352: 1 / 0.9691
verdicts.note: energy matching is by interpolation over the six bump lifetime runs (no dedicated runs at the S-bend energies); a bump that hops sites is scored by its co-moving frac
